scenes.headline: How a 14 MB model calls tools on tiny devices
scenes.sub: Cactus Needle 2: 45M parameters, 2-bit from pretraining, tuned on your tools.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pistachio! Needle 2 is a forty-five-million-parameter tool caller from Cactus: a fourteen-megabyte file that runs in twenty-eight megabytes of RAM. Here's how it works.

scenes.label: The scoping bet
scenes.text: Tool calling needs no world knowledge: map a messy sentence onto a few typed functions. So shrink the model, then tune it to your tools.
scenes.say: The idea: tool calling needs no world knowledge. It maps a messy sentence onto a few typed functions. So make the model small, then tune it to your tools.

steps.say: A token enters a tied embedding, then climbs twenty-seven blocks, each reading from and writing to four residual lanes.
Engram tables hold eight million parameters of hashed n-grams, read by gathering a few rows, not by a matrix multiply.
Attention looks back only two hundred fifty-six tokens, so memory stays a fixed twenty-eight megabytes instead of growing with the conversation.
At the top, a byte-level grammar constrains decoding into an exact function call.

scenes.title: Trained at two bits, not squeezed to them

left.title: Post-hoc quantization
left.say: Small models usually break when they're quantized after training.

right.title: Cactus Quants from day one
items: Weights, activations and KV cache alike
The deployed model is the trained one
right.say: Needle trains at two bits from pretraining on: weights, activations and cache. The model you deploy is the model that was trained.

scenes.label: lift from fine-tuning on your own tool schemas
scenes.note: ahead of a zero-shot DeepSeek V4 Flash on three of four benchmarks
scenes.say: Tune it on your own schemas, on a laptop, and Cactus reports gains of twenty-one to fifty-eight points, beating a zero-shot frontier model on three of four benchmarks.

scenes.text: Your product has twelve tools, not twelve thousand. A small model tuned on exactly those can beat a generalist.
